target_customer: Product, engineering and data teams at software companies that want feature flags and A/B tests on their own data warehouse
problem: SaaS experimentation tools such as LaunchDarkly make companies send data to a vendor, adding cost, compliance issues and lock in, so many build in house; GrowthBook runs experiments on a company's existing data infrastructure.
business_model: Open source core with paid cloud and enterprise (self hosted or cloud) plans

founders.name: Graham McNicoll
education: Carnegie Mellon University, physics degree (per YC page)
previous_startups: International nonprofit for communication access in developing world (founder)
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a three time founder.

founders.name: Jeremy Dorn
founders.background_notes: YC page says he scaled the Education.com web application to over 1 billion requests per month and is active in open source.

competitors.name: LaunchDarkly
competitors.what: Hosted feature flag SaaS that GrowthBook says requires sending data to the vendor, with high cost and lock in
competitors.traction_then: Established market leader per the YC page positioning
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in sources I opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Statistics engine, SDKs across many languages and warehouse integrations; solid engineering with some hard statistical parts.

defensibility.rationale: Open source adoption, community connectors and warehouse native architecture make it sticky, but code is open and competitors like PostHog and Unleash exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied the warehouse native open source model into a takeover; GrowthBook raised its Series A in 2025 and remains independent.

market_need_then: Companies complained about sending data to LaunchDarkly style vendors and many built tools in house, costing thousands of hours (YC description of the problem).

identity.logo: Text based logo, per the GitHub README
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer and data team focused; tagline: Build smarter. Ship safely. Grow at the speed of AI.

branding.brand_signature: Open source with an active community Slack and GitHub repository
branding.community_and_virality: Company claims thousands of companies and an active Slack community giving feedback; GitHub stars cited at 5,300 or 7,800 depending on source.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear name that says growth plus experiments, backed by open source community pull; no mascot or press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: GrowthBook began as an in house experimentation tool, was open sourced in 2021, and joined YC in Winter 2022 with experienced founders from Education.com. It grew through open source adoption, claims over 4,000 companies on its site, and raised a 22.6M Series A in mid 2025. No acquisition or layoffs were found.
notes: Series A of about 22.62M USD in mid 2025 appears in Seedtable and CB Insights (aggregators); a search summary also says the company's own announcement states 22,620,000, but I did not open it. The lead is disputed: Seedtable and CB Insights say Nava Ventures, another source says Khosla Ventures. A YC seed around 2022-03 is listed by aggregators with conflicting amounts (130K, 7.1M, 8M total), so not recorded as a round. Founding year 2020 is from a search summary; YC page year not seen.
